olivia: heads-up — running into a weird TLS verification failure only when using the async python client against Dedicated + proxy + custom CA bundle. sync client works fine. :thinking:

olivia: error is: `ssl.SSLError: [SSL: CERTIFICATE_VERIFY_FAILED] certificate verify failed: unable to get local issuer certificate` — only when I set REDWOOD_API_BASE to the dedicated base_url and have HTTPS_PROXY set.

raj: which sdk + httpx versions? can you paste a tiny repro?

olivia: redwood-sdk==0.12.5, httpx==0.23.3, python 3.11. repro script:

```
from redwood import AsyncClient

async def main():
    c = AsyncClient(api_key="x", base_url="https://dedicated-123.us.redwood.prod")
    await c.chat.create(model="gpt-mini", input="hi")

# env:
# HTTPS_PROXY=http://proxy.corp:8080
# REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE=/etc/certs/custom-root.pem

```

olivia: running that fails. if I switch to the synchronous client (`Client`) with same env it works.

emily: hmm, sounds like httpx + proxies + custom CA edge case. httpx's async transport might be using a different verify path. did you try setting SSL_CERT_FILE or SSL_CERT_DIR?

olivia: tried SSL_CERT_FILE=/etc/certs/custom-root.pem and still fails for async. sync works.

mike: quick guess: our AsyncClient wrapper sets `trust_env=True` and relies on httpx internals; when CONNECTing through an HTTP proxy httpx may validate the proxy cert (if proxy uses TLS) vs the upstream. if the proxy rewrites or does TLS intercept, verify logic gets messy. can you confirm if proxy is plain http or https?

olivia: proxy is http (not https). so CONNECT to upstream. I captured httpx debug: `Event: connection.handshake ssl.SSLError` and the cert presented looks like the dedicated endpoint cert (so not proxy).

raj: interesting. one more idea: are you passing `verify` anywhere? our async wrapper doesn't expose the underlying `transport` verify parameter. sync client ends up using `requests` which respects REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE. httpx uses different env var semantics (REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE isn't honored by httpx).

emily: yes — httpx does not read REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE. it uses `SSL_CERT_FILE` / `certifi.where()` unless you pass `verify=`. so that explains why sync (requests) sees the bundle but async (httpx) doesn't.

olivia: ohhh. that matches. so my mistake was assuming REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE would work. but I did set SSL_CERT_FILE earlier and it still failed?

mike: did you set SSL_CERT_FILE in the same process (exported before python) or set REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE only? also check if our wrapper spawns a uvloop or separate process where env not inherited.

olivia: exported before running `python -m repro`. same shell. still fails.

raj: can you try a direct httpx snippet forcing verify to the bundle to confirm? e.g.:

```python
import httpx
client = httpx.AsyncClient(verify="/etc/certs/custom-root.pem", proxies={"https": "http://proxy.corp:8080"})
await client.get("https://dedicated-123.us.redwood.prod/ping")
```

raj: if that works, we need to expose verify or allow SDK to pick up SSL_CERT_FILE correctly.

olivia: tried that exact snippet — it succeeds. forcing verify file works. so it is definitely env vs httpx default behavior.

emily: short-term workaround: set `REDWOOD_PY_HTTPX_VERIFY=/etc/certs/custom-root.pem` env and we can update SDK to read it. longer-term: we should update SDK to construct an AsyncHTTPTransport with `verify=` when base_url is a Dedicated host and a custom CA path is detected in env (SSL_CERT_FILE or REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE).

mike: agree. also add a note in onboarding docs: "When using Dedicated behind corp proxies, httpx-based async clients require explicit verify path or SSL_CERT_FILE; REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE is not sufficient."

olivia: I'll open a small PR + issue: repro, docs, and patch to read SSL_CERT_FILE into AsyncClient constructor and pass it to transport.

raj: can you add a unit test that simulates proxies by setting `trust_env=True` and `proxies`? we should avoid altering behavior for normal public hosted users. flag should be opt-in (REDWOOD_PY_HTTPX_VERIFY or detected env).

emily: also add an integration test in CI that runs a tiny httpx client pointing at a local mitmproxy with custom CA to catch regressions.

olivia: ack. I'll add issue/PR and a short note in devex docs. thanks for the quick debugging help :thumbsup:

mike: thanks — this pattern has bitten a few other teams. good to make it explicit in samples.

olivia: action items I will do: create GH issue + repro (code + env), PR to read SSL_CERT_FILE into async transport, update docs samples (sample-apps/dedicated/proxy.md), and add CI test. ETA EOD Thu.

raj: perfect — tag me and emily on the PR for review.

olivia: will do. closing for now.
